fire: The engine produces peak torque at 3,500 rpm.
The spindle turns at up to twelve thousand revolutions per minute.
Keep the drill's rotation speed low when cutting steel.
At idle, the motor runs at about 800 RPM.
The turbine blades spin at a constant rotational speed.
Shift up before the needle passes 6000 rpm.
The record player supports both 33 and 45 rpm discs.
Reduce the fan's revolutions per minute to cut the noise.
quiet: The engine produces peak torque on steep hills.
The spindle is made of hardened tool steel.
Keep the drill's battery charged when cutting steel.
At idle, the motor makes a soft humming sound.
The turbine blades are coated to resist corrosion.
Shift up before the road starts to climb.
The record player supports both vinyl and shellac discs.
Reduce the fan's dust buildup to cut the noise.
